_note: Authoring skeleton. Files whose name starts with _ are skipped by build.py, validate.py, coverage.py and similarity_check.py. Three examples follow: (1) a standard extended-response item, (2) an MCQ cluster for Physics P1A, (3) a data-based item for Physics P1B. Copy whichever matches the paper you are writing for.

questions.subject: Math AA HL
questions.syllabus_ref: AHL 5.18 (first order differential equations; integrating factor)
questions.challenge_mechanism: Name the single mechanism that makes this hard, in one full sentence. 'Multi-step' is not a mechanism. Say what the student has to notice, reject, or invert.
questions.question: The stem. Sets the scene, gives the data, and introduces anything a later part refers back to.

parts.label: a
parts.text: A complete, self-contained sub-question. At least eight words.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Each part must depend on the previous one, or at least be useless without it.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Part marks must sum exactly to the marks field.

questions.answer: Full worked solution. Every award annotated (M1)(A1)(R1)(AG) at the point it is earned. Aim well above 190 words for maths, 440 for CS.
questions.markscheme_notes: Alternative methods, condonations, follow-through, and what forfeits a mark. Minimum 125 words.
questions.explanation: The key insight, why the question is hard, and the classic wrong turns. Minimum 195 words for maths.

provenance.adaptation: Required unless inspired_by is 'original'. State what was borrowed and what changed.

verification.method: How every number was checked: analytic recompute, numerical solve, code executed, or hand trace.
solution_skeleton: state the physical or mathematical model being assumed
derive the governing relation from that model
check the result against a limiting case

questions.subject: Physics HL
questions.topic: Theme A: Space, time and motion
questions.challenge_mechanism: One sentence naming the discriminating step. For MCQ this is usually the move that separates the correct option from the strongest distractor, not simply 'it is multi-step'.
questions.question: Optional shared preamble for the cluster. Each MCQ below is self-contained and answerable on its own, as in a real Paper 1A.

parts.label: a
parts.text: A self-contained multiple-choice question. No reference to other parts.

options.label: A
options.text: The correct option, written in the same register as the others.
options.rationale: Why this is right, stated as a complete line of reasoning, not just 'correct substitution'.

options.label: B
options.text: A distractor that encodes a specific, predictable error.
options.rationale: Name the error: e.g. 'uses the diameter where the radius is required'. Every distractor must be there for a reason.

options.label: C
options.text: A distractor from a sign, unit or proportionality slip.

options.label: D
options.text: A distractor from applying a valid formula in the wrong regime.
options.rationale: Name why the formula does not apply here.

questions.answer: Worked solution for every MCQ in the cluster, in order. For each: the shortest reliable route to the answer, the value, and why the nearest distractor is wrong. Annotate (A1) at the point the correct option is fixed.
questions.markscheme_notes: One mark per MCQ, no negative marking. Note any option that is condoned, any that require a unit conversion, and the common elimination route a strong student would use.
questions.explanation: What the cluster discriminates. Name the misconception each distractor targets and why a guessing student is unlikely to land on the key.

provenance.adaptation: Original. Distractor set designed from the known error patterns for this subtopic.

verification.method: Each option recomputed independently in Python to full precision; distractors verified to be the result of the named error.
solution_skeleton: identify the conserved quantity or governing law
express the target in terms of given quantities
compute and match to an option

questions.subject: Physics HL
questions.topic: Theme A: Space, time and motion
questions.challenge_mechanism: One sentence: what the data hides. Typically the relationship is only visible after a non-obvious linearisation, or one row is anomalous and must be defended rather than discarded.

stimulus.title: Student investigation
stimulus.body: Describe the apparatus and method in the past tense, as a student report. Include the controlled variables and the measurement resolution of each instrument, because later parts will ask about them.

table.caption: Measured values, with units in the column headers.

questions.question: Short lead-in. The data and the method are in the stimulus.

parts.label: a
parts.text: State the uncertainty in a quantity derived from two instruments in series, with a reason.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Describe how a resolution limit can be beaten by repeating or by timing over N intervals.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Linearise the proposed relationship, determine the constant from the gradient, and give its unit.

parts.label: d
parts.text: Evaluate whether the data support the model, referring to a specific anomalous row.

questions.answer: Worked answers with (M1)(A1)(R1) where earned. Gradient taken from widely separated points on the best-fit line, not adjacent table rows. Units carried through.
questions.markscheme_notes: Allow the alternative linearisation. Note where follow-through applies from an earlier part and what forfeits the unit mark.
questions.explanation: What the question is really testing: usually that the student must choose the transformation, not be told it.

provenance.adaptation: Original dataset generated from the model with deliberate scatter and one seeded anomaly.

verification.method: Dataset generated in Python from the stated model with known parameters, then rounded to the instrument resolution; the seeded anomaly confirmed to fall outside the residuals.
solution_skeleton: combine instrument uncertainties for the derived quantity
take the gradient from separated best-fit points
compare the intercept and residuals against the model
